title: The Trumpeter Taken Prisoner
text:
In the middle of a battle, a trumpeter who had been sounding the charge and urging his side forward was cut off and captured by the enemy.

He pleaded for his life. He told his captors that he had done them no harm at all. He had not killed a single one of their men. He carried no sword or spear, nothing but his brass trumpet, so it would be unjust to put him to death.

The soldiers were not moved. That, they told him, was exactly why he deserved to die. He might never strike a blow himself, but every time he raised the trumpet to his lips he sent others rushing in to strike for him. A man who stirs up a whole army is more dangerous than any single fighter in it.
lesson: Words that move others to act carry responsibility for what those others do. If you rally people, you own the results of the rally, even if your own hands stay clean.
